notes: Core and mobility work performed post-session (10 minutes at the end of every training session)
Weeks 3–4: Introduce supersets on isolation work — Lateral Raise superset with Tricep Pushdown; Hammer Curl superset with Face Pull; Leg Curl superset with Calf Raise
Weeks 7–8: Introduce drop sets on final set of one isolation exercise per session (lateral raises, EZ bar curl, leg curl) — drop 30% and continue to failure
Weeks 11–12: Introduce rest-pause sets on final set of each primary compound — complete target reps, rest 15 seconds, squeeze out 2–3 more reps
Weeks 11–12: Mechanical drop set on legs — Bulgarian Split Squat immediately into Reverse Lunge immediately into Goblet Squat, reducing load each movement
Week 12 final 3 days: Reduce volume by 30% (drop one set per exercise), maintain intensity — mini-deload
Progressive overload target: add 2.5 kg to compound lifts or 1 additional rep per set each week
Weeks 3–4: Add 1 working set to all compound movements (bench, squat, RDL, row) — now 4 sets
Weeks 7–8: Add 1 additional set to all compound movements — now 5 sets on primary compounds
Phase 1 rest periods: 60–90 seconds between sets
Phase 2 rest periods: 90–120 seconds on compounds, 60 seconds on isolations
Phase 3 rest periods: 2–3 minutes on compounds, 60–90 seconds on isolations
Protein spread across 4–5 meals rather than loading into 1–2 sittings
Minimum 30–35g protein per meal to adequately stimulate muscle protein synthesis
Pre-workout nutrition 60–90 minutes before training: prioritise carbohydrates and moderate protein
Post-workout nutrition within 60 minutes: prioritise protein and carbohydrates
Begin tracking 1RM estimates on bench, squat, and RDL at weeks 7–8 to set Phase 3 percentages
Reassess at week 4 and week 8 — adjust loads, note movement compensations, check nutrition adherence
Active recovery options on rest days: 20–30 minute walk, light yoga/stretching, swimming (easy pace), foam rolling

# 12-Week Muscle Gain Programme
### Client Profile: 26F | Vegan | Recreational Lifter | Goal: Hypertrophy

---

## PROGRAMME PHILOSOPHY

This programme runs across **three four-week phases**, each building on the last in volume, intensity, and complexity. The training split is a **Push / Pull / Legs (PPL)** structure run on a **6-day rotating schedule** (3 days on, 1 day off, or 2 on / 1 off / 2 on / 1 off depending on lifestyle), giving each muscle group direct stimulus twice per week. The seventh day is full rest or active recovery.

Progressive overload is the central driver: each week she should aim to add **2.5 kg to compound lifts** or **1 additional rep per set** before adding weight. Log every session.

---

## PHASE 1 — FOUNDATION (Weeks 1–4)
**Goal:** Establish movement patterns, build work capacity, introduce progressive overload, and prime connective tissue.
**Rep ranges:** 10–15 | **RPE target:** 6–7 | **Rest:** 60–90 seconds between sets

---

### WEEK 1–2 TEMPLATE

#### SESSION A — PUSH (Chest / Shoulders / Triceps)

| Exercise | Sets | Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Barbell Bench Press | 3 | 12 | Focus on controlled eccentric (3 sec down) |
| Dumbbell Shoulder Press | 3 | 12 | Neutral grip option if shoulder discomfort |
| Incline Dumbbell Fly | 3 | 15 | Light weight, full stretch at bottom |
| Lateral Raise | 3 | 15 | Slight forward lean, lead with elbow |
| Tricep Rope Pushdown | 3 | 15 | Elbows pinned to sides |
| Overhead Tricep Extension (DB) | 3 | 12 | Full range, feel the long head stretch |

---

#### SESSION B — PULL (Back / Biceps / Rear Delts)

| Exercise | Sets | Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lat Pulldown (wide grip) | 3 | 12 | Depress scapula before pulling |
| Seated Cable Row (close grip) | 3 | 12 | Drive elbows back, squeeze at end |
| Dumbbell Single-Arm Row | 3 | 12 each | Brace core, full ROM |
| Face Pull (rope) | 3 | 15 | External rotation emphasis |
| Dumbbell Hammer Curl | 3 | 12 | Controlled, no swinging |
| Incline Dumbbell Curl | 3 | 12 | Supinated, long head bias |

---

#### SESSION C — LEGS (Quads / Hamstrings / Glutes / Calves)

| Exercise | Sets | Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Barbell Back Squat | 3 | 12 | Depth to parallel or below |
| Romanian Deadlift (RDL) | 3 | 12 | Hip hinge, soft knee, feel hamstring load |

## NUTRITION PLAN — 150g PROTEIN/DAY FROM PLANT SOURCES

### Calorie Target
For muscle gain, she should be in a **modest caloric surplus of 250–350 kcal above maintenance**. For a 26-year-old active female, estimated maintenance sits around **2,000–2,200 kcal** depending on body weight and NEAT. A reasonable starting target is:

> **2,400–2,500 kcal/day**

Adjust after 3 weeks based on scale weight and body composition feedback. Aim for **0.25–0.5 kg gain per month** — slow enough to minimise fat gain.

---

| **Protein** | **150g (600 kcal)** |
| **Carbohydrates** | **280–300g (1,120–1,200 kcal)** |
| **Fat** | **70–80g (630–720 kcal)** |

**Key principle:** Combine protein sources across the day to ensure a **complete amino acid profile**, particularly adequate **leucine** (the primary trigger for muscle protein synthesis). Leucine is lower in most plant foods, so volume and variety matter. Pea protein and soy are the most leucine-rich plant options.

### Nutrient Timing

- **Pre-workout (60–90 min before):** Prioritise carbohydrates for fuel and moderate protein — the edamame + fruit snack above is ideal
- **Post-workout (within 60 minutes):** Prioritise protein + carbohydrates to maximise muscle protein synthesis — the lentil/chickpea dinner works well here
- **Spread protein across 4–5 meals** rather than loading it into 1–2 sittings — plant proteins have slightly lower digestibility, so distribution matters more than with animal sources
- **Minimum 30–35g protein per meal** to adequately stimulate muscle protein synthesis given lower leucine content of plant foods

---

### Key Supplements (Vegan-Specific)

These are not optional extras — several address genuine gaps in a vegan diet that directly affect muscle gain and recovery:

| Supplement | Dose | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| **Creatine Monohydrate** | 3–5g daily | Proven for strength and hypertrophy; not found in plant foods |
| **Vitamin B12** | 1,000 mcg daily (or 2,500 mcg 3×/week) | Essential; completely absent from plant foods |
| **Vitamin D3 (vegan)** | 2,000–4,000 IU daily | Muscle function, immune health; most people are deficient |
| **Omega-3 (Algae Oil)** | 250–500mg EPA+DHA daily | Anti-inflammatory; fish get it from algae — cut out the middleman |
| **Iodine** | 150 mcg daily | Often low in vegan diets; thyroid and metabolic function |
| **Zinc** | 8–11mg daily | Testosterone, recovery; absorption is lower from plant sources |
| **Pea or Soy Protein Powder** | 1–2 scoops daily | Practical tool to hit protein targets |

*Advise her to get a blood panel at the start and at week 12 to check B12, D, iron, and ferritin levels.*

## RECOVERY PROTOCOL

### Sleep
Target **7.5–9 hours per night**. Growth hormone is predominantly released during deep sleep. Poor sleep directly blunts muscle protein synthesis and increases cortisol.

### Active Recovery (Rest Days)
Choose one or two of the following:
- 20–30 minute walk
- Light yoga or stretching (YouTube vinyasa flow)
- Swimming (easy pace)
- Foam rolling — focus on quads, hamstrings, lats, and thoracic spine (10 minutes)

### Hydration
- Minimum **2.5–3 litres of water daily**
- Add an extra 500ml on training days
- Electrolytes (sodium, potassium, magnesium) are important — a pinch of sea salt in water post-session is a simple fix

### Stress Management
Chronic stress elevates cortisol, which is catabolic (muscle-wasting). Encourage:
- 5–10 minutes of breathwork or meditation daily (apps: Calm, Headspace)
- Limiting caffeine after 2pm to protect sleep quality

## TRAINER NOTES

- **Reassess at week 4 and week 8** — adjust loads, note any movement compensations, and check in on nutrition adherence
- If she struggles to hit 150g protein in early weeks, **prioritise the two post-workout meals** and use protein powder strategically — don't let perfect be the enemy of good
- Watch for signs of **under-recovery** in Phase 3: persistent soreness, declining performance, disrupted sleep, or mood changes — reduce volume before reducing intensity
- Seitan is the highest-protein plant food by weight but contains gluten — confirm she has no sensitivity before recommending it heavily
- **Soy foods (tofu, edamame, tempeh)** are the gold standard for vegan muscle gain due to their complete amino acid profile and leucine content — encourage daily inclusion
